units.title: Title, outline, and module intended learning outcomes
units.summary: AS114206 HD in Rehabilitation Services AS114206J HHS3190M Human Physiology and Functional Anatomy for Rehabilitation Services HHS3190MJ Semester 1 (26-27) Scheme of Module Activity Outline ▪ Module Intended Learning Outcomes (MILO) ▪ Module Assessment Plan ▪ Lesson Plan Module Intended Learning Outcomes (MILO) On completion of this module, learners are expected to be able to: 1. Describe the mechanism of human body in maintaining a normal homeostasis or accomplishing a particular task essential for life with reference to the functions of various body systems regarding the rehabilitation industry. Explain the consequences of different various physiological disorders with appropriate mechanisms in account of rehabilitation aspects. Identify, classify and describe the musculoskeletal structures of the human body in standard terminologies in rehabilitation perspective. Illustrate the interaction between responsible musculoskeletal structures of human body involving in the complex functional movements in rehabilitation perspective.

units.title: Module assessment plan and pass requirements
units.summary: Module Assessment Plan In order to pass this module, a student must: (a) attain at least 70% attendance at the end of this module in semester 2; and (b) pass End-of-Module Assessment (EA) by attaining at least 40% of overall EA mark in semester 2; and (c) attain at least 40% of overall module mark. Assessment items will be conducted in semester 1 and 2. Assessments of Physiology Part • CA Physiology Tutorial Exercises will be explained and conducted in semester 1 tutorial lessons. Student must complete and submit the exercises to teacher within designated period. Late submission before disclosure of the answers will lead to mark deduction.
